ANDROID-01.impact: - `android/mesh/src/main/java/io/godstone/mesh/transport/BleTransport.kt:312` handles the successful central CCCD action by publishing `Found`, then stops. It does not call `beginTrustedHandshake`. - `BleTransport.kt:1739` defines `beginTrustedHandshake`. Searching both `android/mesh/src/main` and `android/app/src/main` finds its definition and no invocation (`production_entrypoints.txt`). Existing tests call it explicitly, e.g. `ReadinessT21Test.kt:321`. - `BleTransport.kt:1353` defines `beginKeyConfirmation`; every invocation found outside its definition is a test invocation (`keyconfirmation_callers.txt`). Completing HS3 at lines 1566/1623 only emits `handshakeReadyFlow`. - `MeshNode.kt:179` subscribes only to `peers()` and `received()`. It subscribes to neither handshake-ready nor application-link-ready events and does not perform D2/key confirmation itself. Failure schedule: two genuine devices finish discovery, LinkInfo exchange, and CCCD setup. The central produces `PublishFound`; no HS1 is sent. The responder cannot initiate Noise XX. Both remain physically bound without a trusted session. If a test or later caller manually starts D2, nothing automatically begins the mandatory encrypted confirmation round afterward.
ANDROID-01.notes: ENRICHED AT ROUND 104 by TRANSCRIPTION from the audit's own card (android/findings.md#ANDROID-01): impact, remediation_steps, source_refs and closure_tests are the card's OWN words and its OWN file references, not a summary; the refs are relative to the audited snapshot. No status changed and nothing was claimed fixed.
remediation_steps: Add one internal effect for the exact successful outbound relation generation, e.g. `BeginHandshake(RelationKey)`, in the relation owner. Trigger it exactly once after ROLE_BOUND and physical duplex are both true.
Capture the remote LinkInfo hint from that same relation (see ANDROID-02). Pass the captured relation and hint to the asynchronous handshake send path. Do not publish an application peer here.

On the real HS3 ordered-write/trust transition, schedule one encrypted confirmation challenge per relation through the record writer. Treat failure/backpressure as an owned pending effect or terminal transition; do not ignore it.
On a valid authenticated response, publish the immutable trusted peer through the T24 channel. Keep HS3-before-DATA ordering and readiness flags false.
Remove the requirement that application/test code directly invoke D2 to make a connection progress.
ANDROID-01.title: The application never starts D2 or key confirmation

ANDROID-02.impact: A canonically-advertising (UUID-only) peer could never complete the trusted handshake on the Android isle: the scan is admitted, the GATT LinkInfo read binds the roles correctly, HS1 is emitted, an authentic HS2 arrives, and the initiator then closes before HS3 with `no remembered discovery hint` -- for lack of a hint the advertisement was never obligated to carry. The audit records this as a blocker that REMAINS after ANDROID-01 is fixed.

A `tryEmit` can return true with no subscribers and retain no event; checking its Boolean does not make this a durable/reliable channel. ANDROID-06.impact: Whole-record reservations do not reserve capacity or enforce single consumption: `RecordWriter.reserve` checks only already-SEALED `admitted.size` and returns a ticket without recording outstanding reservations, and `sealAndQueueOf` has no consumed/cancelled ticket check -- it invokes the sealer BEFORE rechecking the full admitted queue. Three reproduced schedules: (1) seal one ticket twice and both calls enqueue with the same operation id and different sequence/nonces, so completions cannot distinguish repeated ticket ownership; (2) reserve five tickets before sealing any and all five are admitted although the whole-record limit is four; (3) hold a reservation, fill the four slots through other reservations, then seal the held one -- the sealer runs (consuming a nonce) before the capacity refusal, so admission was not a guarantee and refusal was not free of cryptographic work.

THE CHEAPEST RED IS ALREADY NAMED, and it is the card's own FAILURE SCHEDULE 2: reserve FIVE tickets before sealing any, when the configured whole-record limit is FOUR -- the fifth reservation must be REFUSED, and today all five are admitted because `reserve` never counts outstanding reservations. THE DEFECT WAS ONE CONDITIONAL AWAY FROM A CORRECT GATE on both isles: `if key != nil { verify }` converted a temporary resolution failure into a durable VERIFIED_RECIPIENT row and a retired obligation. The Android red failed at its FIRST assertion -- the counter that should have recorded unavailability recorded ZERO, because the code never treated resolution failure as unavailability; the iOS red failed five times, ending with the obligation not surviving. WHAT REMAINS IS THE COMPLEMENTARY CONTROL the audit names, not a second repair: a present-but-WRONG key must be refused as a mismatch rather than folded into unavailability, and the explicit NodeID derivation is prescribed in form. ROUND 77: the audit's step-1 control was added on BOTH isles in one pass and it PASSES everywhere (keyUnavailable 0, storageFailures 1, nothing stored, obligation survives), so the repair's two branches are now both witnessed -- the arm that went red and the control that protects what the repair did not touch. ROUND 78: THE AUDIT'S STEP 3 IS DONE IN FORM -- the pinned key must now be 32 bytes AND must derive the claimed recipient's node id under the frozen BLAKE2s128 binding, with the three failure classes (unresolvable / malformed / mismatched) separately enforced and separately witnessed. Combined with round 77's control, steps 1 and 3 of this finding's remediation list are complete on both isles. ONE MECHANICAL CORRECTION: the first Android form referenced a constant whose insertion did not land, so the size check is a literal 32 with its comment; the compile error was the correction. ROUND 83: STEP 4 OF THIS FINDING'S REMEDIATION LIST IS CLOSED AS SATISFIED BY CONSTRUCTION -- the verifier cannot take a caller-supplied key; it resolves the pinned key for the expected recipient from the same resolver the worker captured it from, so the two cannot differ. That was verified in the source (AckAuthenticator.kt:120-142) rather than assumed, and it is recorded WITH the caveat that no court directly proves the verifier cannot be induced to use a different key (the round-77 wrong-key control is the closest evidence). No code was changed for this step and none is warranted: a red for it is impossible. ROUND 86: the audit's ordered STEP 4 is LANDED ON BOTH ISLES, and it was a REAL hole -- round 83's 'satisfied by construction' was wrong, and re-reading the store is what showed it. `AckObligationStore` resolveth the pinned key ONCE and GATES on it (size 32, and `nodeIdOf(key) == claimed`) and then asked for a verification that RESOLVED THE KEY AGAIN: the key that was validated and the key that was used were two different calls, so a resolver whose answer changed between them had a frame signed under its LATER answer filed as VERIFIED_RECIPIENT while the gate certified the earlier one. The red proved it with an ATTACKER-SUPPLIED frame on the ADMISSION road: `Stored(ackKey=...)` before the repair. THE FIX, chosen for blast radius: a defaulted `verifyWithCapturedKey(...)` on the `AckAuthenticator` interface (delegating to `verify`, so every double in the mandatory lanes keeps compiling; the Swift isle uses a protocol-extension default for the same reason), overridden in `Ed25519AckAuthenticator` to (a) fail closed when the resolver no longer names the captured key and (b) run the signature check under the CAPTURED key; `verify`'s signature was NOT changed, and both store call sites now pass the key they gated. A WITHDRAWN FIRST ARM IS RECORDED IN THE COURT: the first attempt drove the RESTART road with the signer seam handing the attacker's seed and came back GREEN on the pre-repair revision -- it isolated nothing, because that seam never signs a frame the gate would distrust. The forged frame must arrive through the ADMISSION road, where the bytes are attacker-supplied. AND A REGRESSION THIS ROUND CAUSED, CAUGHT BY THE FULL LANE AND CORRECTED: the first refactor resolved the pinned key BEFORE the structural guards, which broke a PINNED pre-resolver-guard law -- BoundRecipientKeyResolverTest.testBoundResolver_AckIntegration_PreResolverGuards_ZeroLookup requireth ZERO key lookups for a wrong expected recipient ('expected:<0> but was:<1>'). A view that navigateth directly skippeth EVERY one of those: no epoch, no retry token, no staleness gate, no failure publication -- which is exactly the navigation-bypasses-selection-metadata finding. THE CANDIDATE EDIT (NOT APPLIED): route the destination through the owner, e.g. keep the `navigationDestination` but drive it with `.task { await scene.open(document: document) }` so the SCENE selecteth, and make the reader render the scene's phase/model state rather than loading on its own. WHY IT WAS NOT APPLIED THIS ROUND, PLAINLY: the reader's own body (from `ArchiveView.swift:143`) has NOT been read, so a blind edit could just as easily DOUBLE-LOAD the document as fix it; and the ios lane costeth ~138 SECONDS plus a mirror sync, so an edit could not be both made and verified in what remained of this round. STEP 1 REFINED (round 125, still NO EDIT): THE READER IS NOT MERELY A VIEW THAT FORGETTETH THE SCENE -- IT HOLDS A SECOND LOADING PATH. `ios/Godstone/Sources/App/ArchiveView.swift:143-157` `ArchiveDocumentReader` owneth `@StateObject private var model: ArchiveReaderModel` (built from the LIBRARY), so the DOCUMENT CONTENT is loaded by a model the scene knoweth nothing about, while the SAME view already consumeth the scene for `scrollAnchor?.passageId` (the GS-ARCHIVE-004 anchor) and for `openedSource`/`openedDocumentId` (the provenance line). The earlier reading -- 65 non-ascending draws being 'statistically impossible', therefore shared RNG state -- was WRONG, and the correction is the point: the fixture in ReadinessT17Test and ReadinessT18Test redrew `b` ALONE against a FIXED `a`, so a draw was accepted with probability (255 - a.hint[0])/256, NOT one half. With a.hint[0] = 254 (1 call in 256) each redraw needed the 1/256 case b.hint[0] == 255, so sixty-five draws failed with probability ~78%. MEASURED, not guessed: the two loops were instrumented in a DETACHED WORKTREE of 5e87add (production byte-identical to it) and the filtered courts were run repeatedly, catching 'FLAKE-PROBE FAILED draws=65 a=254,25,59,239 b=67,174,80,195 identical=false aIdEqBId=false' in testAttestTwentyTwentyCarriesTheFullDigest, with NINE of THIRTY runs failing, all in FIXTURE SETUP. The other five courts (T20, T21, T22 x2, T23) redraw BOTH identities, so their acceptance probability is ~1/2 per draw and their 65-draw failure is genuinely impossible -- which is exactly why only these two courts ever flaked, and why they alone were changed. The repair ORDERS the drawn pair by hint instead of fishing on the coin (and fails with a message naming the two hints only if they are equal, a 2^-32 collision). GS-INBOX-001.impact: A peer that has seen a message ID can send a corrupted relay copy first. A later genuine delivery can be acknowledged to the sender without persisting its actual content. A restart then loses the genuine local message although the sender may accept DELIVERED. Generic relay eviction also cannot stand in for a durable user inbox/tombstone. This is a storage-proof failure, not a forged recipient signature; current missing composition/readiness gates remain separate blockers.
remediation_steps: First retain the failing probe as a regression on both platforms. Do not fix it by weakening the expected stored payload or by treating a valid signature in RAM as durable receipt.

Add a versioned inbox_messages table and inbox_dedup/tombstone representation in the runtime-owned private database, separate from held_frames. The inbox row must pin msgID, verified author and local recipient, canonical signed content (or an equivalently reconstructible protected representation), content digest, first local receipt, remaining lifetime, and identity generation. Use the encrypted-store work from GS-STORE-001/002 and preserve existing rows through migration (GS-STORE-003).

Change the commit boundary from a raw frame-only closure to a verified input type, built only after SignedMessageV1.verify and sender-policy admission. The existing VerifiedApplicationMessage can supply the authenticated fields. Keep receivedFrom separately as immediate-hop metadata; it is not the author.

Inside one real store transaction: check the verified inbox key; on absence insert the protected verified content plus the dedup record; on presence require the pinned author/recipient/content identity to match; then insert the pending ACK obligation. Commit all three together. A conflicting relay row must neither satisfy nor veto the verified inbox proof.

Return New or Duplicate based on the verified inbox/tombstone, never generic relay membership. A mismatch in an existing verified inbox row must return a typed conflict/corruption result with no ACK and no destructive overwrite. If a generic held copy needs replacement, do it only after its relation to the verified message is explicitly checked.

Keep relay custody and eviction independent. Relay capacity eviction must not remove accepted user inbox content or the dedup proof while its retention obligation is active. Extend quotas, retention, schema validation and wipe enumeration to the new durable namespace.
Generate/restore the ACK only after this transaction returns an authoritative committed verified-inbox result. On disk/full/key/corruption/commit failure leave acceptance unclaimed and emit no ACK.

Define the unavoidable in-flight boundary explicitly: bytes already submitted may finish and are reported as possibly relayed; queued work that has not crossed submission must be removable. Do not imply global retraction.

IOS-07.impact: Handshake and key-confirmation deadlines are inspected at inbound DATA/HS ingress (`BleTransport.swift:2963–3001` and `3961–3994`). The public `sweepInboundLeases` (2734) has no caller anywhere in canonical Sources; it sweeps assembly leases, not the handshake/confirmation deadlines. At physical duplex the provisional timer is cancelled (3186), and inbound subscription cancels its timer (3427). `HandshakeDeadline` and `KeyConfirmation` store/check clock values but schedule no timer. Consequently a peer that sends nothing after HS1 or after receiving the challenge need not trigger timeout teardown at all. A stalled partial assembly likewise needs another ingress or an externally invoked sweep.
IOS-07.notes: ENRICHED AT ROUND 104 by TRANSCRIPTION from the audit's own card (ios/findings.md#IOS-07): impact, remediation_steps, source_refs and closure_tests are the card's OWN words and its OWN file references, not a summary; the refs are relative to the audited snapshot. No status changed and nothing was claimed fixed.
remediation_steps: Extend the existing exact-key timer lease mechanism with relation-owned handshake, assembly and confirmation deadline operations, each carrying transport epoch, relation generation, operation id and absolute monotonic deadline.

Arm handshake timeout at ROLE_BOUND without silently extending it on retries. Arm the fixed assembly lease on the first accepted fragment and confirmation timeout when the challenge is committed to the outbound record.

Fire each timeout on its captured manager context's executor; revalidate the full operation key before touching state. Close/drop only that owning relation and its SessionSlot/writer/assemblies. Never resolve a stale fire by looking up the newest relation for a UUID.
Cancel owned timers on success/disconnect/stop and ensure cancellation of an old lease cannot cancel a replacement. Keep existing ingress checks as defense in depth, not the sole timer mechanism.
